references.title: Modelling and worldwide assessment of performance and aging of photovoltaic modules and systems
references.note: Primary scientific reference for this repository. University of Ljubljana catalogue: COBISS 77808131; national-library URN:NBN:SI:DOC-TMG3QFI9. Defended 21 September 2021. Marko Topič is the advisor, not a coauthor. No thesis DOI has been verified. Citation does not claim that every thesis chapter is implemented. CCYA implementation follows sections 7.5.1–7.5.3 (pp. 150–164), with equations 3.6/3.8 for thermal context. The institutional full text is https://repozitorij.uni-lj.si/Dokument.php?id=148326&lang=eng. Explicit choices for monthly centroid scaling, incremental temperature normalization, nonexceedance quantiles and cumulative ratio versus signed gain are documented in docs/ccya.md; no numerical reproduction of Bolzano is claimed.
references.institution: University of Ljubljana, Faculty of Electrical Engineering

references.title: CRU-TS Version 4.10
authors: Climatic Research Unit, University of East Anglia
references.note: Pinned release cruts.2604091129.v4.10, monthly 1901-2025 at 0.5 degrees over land excluding Antarctica. No version DOI was provided on the verified release page. Provider asks users to prefer CEDA and use UEA if CEDA is unavailable or the release has not yet been published there. ODbL with Database Contents License, attribution and share-alike. TMP is monthly mean temperature; PRE is monthly total; PET remains mm/day.

references.title: Global Climate Data Processing and Mapping of Degradation Mechanisms and Degradation Rates of PV Modules
references.note: Source of climate-driven mechanism mapping and 0.2 percent/year categories, also presented in thesis Section 6.4. This implementation requires explicit module calibration and stress conventions. Mean daily extrema and arithmetic ambient humidity in the optional hourly processor are declared adaptations; the published global rasters and their calibration are not claimed reproduced.

references.title: Modeling Outdoor Service Lifetime Prediction of PV Modules: Effects of Combined Climatic Stressors on PV Module Power Degradation
references.note: Original hydrolysis, photodegradation, thermomechanical and multiplicative combined-rate equations (3)-(7), reproduced in thesis equations 3.14-3.17. Publication Boltzmann constant and normalization placement retained. Calibration and climatic aggregation must be supplied explicitly; no universal module coefficients, power-loss trajectory or service-lifetime predictor are implied.

references.title: Assessing the outdoor operating temperature of photovoltaic modules
references.note: Faiman heat-loss temperature model. This implementation follows the 2019 global mapping paper's GHI approximation; it is not a plane-of-array irradiance model.
references.publication: Progress in Photovoltaics: Research and Applications

references.title: Estimating PV Module Performance over Large Geographical Regions: The Role of Irradiance, Air Temperature, Wind Speed and Solar Spectrum
references.note: Source cited by the 2019 mapping study for open-rack crystalline-silicon Faiman coefficients u0=26.9 and u1=6.2 and wind-height scaling exponent 0.2.

references.title: A simple algorithm for the computation of the spectral distribution of the solar irradiance at surface
references.note: UVA/UVB clearness-index regressions, as reproduced in the 2019 degradation mapping paper equations 5–8. The implementation clamps kt to 0.1–0.7 and documents missing/zero-TOA handling.

references.title: Photovoltaic Lifetime Forecast: Models for long-term photovoltaic degradation prediction and forecast
references.note: Author-accessible verification of the 2019 Kaaya model coefficients: Table 4.3, printed p.45 / PDF p.55. Gran Canaria mono-Si calibration: Ah=4.91e7, Eh=0.74, n=1.90; Ap=71.83, Ep=0.45, x=0.63; Atm=2.04, Etm=0.43, theta=2.24. A_N=1 and the applied analysis aggregation/cycling conventions are explicit study choices, not newly fitted coefficients.
